coder.spec: Shrink the MLP hidden width from 4x to 3x the embedding width. In MLP.__init__ both c_fc and c_proj use 4 * config.n_embd as the hidden size; change both to 3 * config.n_embd. forward and init_weights need no change.
coder.title: MLP hidden width 3x

coder.spec: Normalise both residual branches before they are added back. In Block.forward wrap the attention branch output and the MLP branch output in norm(): x = x + norm(self.attn(norm(x), ve, cos_sin, window_size)) and x = x + norm(self.mlp(norm(x))).
coder.title: Normalise both residual branches

coder.spec: Run attention and the MLP in parallel on the same normalised input (GPT-J style) instead of in sequence. In Block.forward compute h = norm(x) once and set x = x + self.attn(h, ve, cos_sin, window_size) + self.mlp(h), so the MLP no longer sees the attention output.
coder.title: Parallel attention and MLP

coder.spec: Remove the x0 skip connection. At the start of every block in GPT.forward the line x = self.resid_lambdas[i] * x + self.x0_lambdas[i] * x0 mixes the embedding output back in; drop the x0 term so the line becomes x = self.resid_lambdas[i] * x. Leave x0_lambdas, init_weights and setup_optimizer alone (the parameter simply gets no gradient).
coder.title: Remove the x0 skip

coder.spec: Apply rotary embeddings to only the first half of each head's channels (partial rotary). Rewrite apply_rotary_emb: with hd = x.shape[3], rotate the channels x[..., :hd // 2] using the first hd // 4 entries of cos and sin (cos and sin have hd // 2 entries in their last dimension), and concatenate the remaining untouched channels x[..., hd // 2:] unchanged at the end. The output keeps the shape (B, T, H, hd). Callers need no change.
coder.title: Partial rotary embeddings

coder.spec: Switch to grouped-query attention with half as many key/value heads as query heads: in build_model_config pass n_kv_head=max(1, num_heads // 2) instead of n_kv_head=num_heads. The model code already supports n_kv_head < n_head (c_k, c_v, ve_gate and the value embeddings are sized from n_kv_head), so nothing else changes.
coder.title: Grouped-query attention

coder.spec: Add a z-loss on the output logits to keep their scale in check. In GPT.forward, after the cross entropy, add 1e-4 * torch.logsumexp(logits, dim=-1).square().mean() to the loss, but only when reduction == 'mean'. The evaluation calls forward with reduction='none' and must keep getting plain per-token cross entropy.
coder.title: Z-loss on the logits

coder.spec: Use a fixed attention softmax scale of 0.12 instead of the default 1/sqrt(head_dim): pass softmax_scale=0.12 to fa3.flash_attn_func in CausalSelfAttention.forward, keeping causal=True and window_size=window_size.
coder.title: Fixed attention scale 0.12

coder.spec: Normalise the value vectors. In CausalSelfAttention.forward, right after the value-embedding block (the if ve is not None: block) and before the rotary embedding, add v = norm(v) at the method's top indentation level so it applies whether or not the layer has a value embedding.
expect: v = norm\(v\)\s+(cos, sin = cos_sin\s+)?q, k = apply_rotary_emb|cos, sin = cos_sin\s+v = norm\(v\)\s+q, k = apply_rotary_emb
coder.title: Normalise the values

coder.spec: Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 before every optimizer update, inside MuonAdamW.step: at the top of step collect all parameters that have a gradient from self.param_groups and call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(params, 1.0). The training loop and the fused update functions stay as they are.
coder.title: Gradient clipping in the optimizer step

coder.spec: Switch Muon from Nesterov to plain momentum. In muon_step_fused the line g = stacked_grads.lerp_(momentum_buffer, momentum) builds the Nesterov-corrected gradient; replace it with g = momentum_buffer so the orthogonalisation works on the momentum buffer itself. Everything else in the function and in MuonAdamW stays.
coder.title: Muon without Nesterov

coder.spec: Make Muon's decoupled weight decay uncautious. In muon_step_fused delete the mask line (mask = (g * stacked_params) >= 0) and apply the decay to every element: the final update becomes stacked_params.sub_(lr * g + lr * wd * stacked_params). The rest of the function stays.
coder.title: Uncautious Muon weight decay

coder.spec: Remove the aspect-ratio scaling of the Muon learning rate. In MuonAdamW._step_muon the line self._muon_lr_t.fill_(group["lr"] * max(1.0, shape[-2] / shape[-1])**0.5) scales the learning rate of tall matrices; make it self._muon_lr_t.fill_(group["lr"]) so every matrix group uses its lr as given.
coder.title: No aspect-ratio scaling of the Muon lr

coder.spec: Make the x0 skip weights per-channel. x0_lambdas is currently one scalar per layer; make it a (n_layer, n_embd) parameter by changing its allocation in GPT.__init__ to nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(config.n_layer, config.n_embd)). The forward pass (self.x0_lambdas[i] * x0) and init_weights (fill_(0.1)) already broadcast correctly, and setup_optimizer puts the parameter in an AdamW group, so only that one line changes.
coder.title: Per-channel x0 skip weights

coder.spec: Initialise the attention input projections orthogonally instead of uniformly: in GPT.init_weights replace the three torch.nn.init.uniform_ calls for block.attn.c_q.weight, c_k.weight and c_v.weight with torch.nn.init.orthogonal_ calls (default gain). The c_proj and MLP initialisation stay as they are.
coder.title: Orthogonal init for q, k, v

coder.spec: Add a learnable gate on each block's contribution to the residual stream. In GPT.__init__ add self.block_gates = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(config.n_layer)). In GPT.forward keep the input of each block and write x = x_in + self.block_gates[i] * (x - x_in) after the block call, so a gate of 1.0 reproduces the current model. The model is built on the meta device, so fill block_gates with 1.0 in GPT.init_weights. block_gates lives outside transformer.h, so setup_optimizer's parameter-count assertion fails until you collect it in a list named gate_params, add that list to the assertion, and give it an AdamW group (lr=scalar_lr * 0.01, betas=adam_betas, eps=1e-10, weight_decay=0.0).
coder.title: Learnable gate per block

coder.spec: Add a learned unigram bias to the output logits. In GPT.__init__ add self.logit_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(config.vocab_size)); in GPT.forward add it to the lm_head output before the float cast and softcap, i.e. logits = self.lm_head(x) + self.logit_bias. The model is built on the meta device, so zero it in GPT.init_weights. logit_bias lives outside transformer.h, so setup_optimizer's parameter-count assertion fails until you collect it in a list named bias_params, add that list to the assertion, and give it an AdamW group (lr=unembedding_lr * dmodel_lr_scale, betas=adam_betas, eps=1e-10, weight_decay=0.0).
coder.title: Learned unigram logit bias

coder.spec: Train the MLP matrices with a larger Muon learning rate than the attention matrices. In GPT.setup_optimizer split the block matrices into attn_params (the parameters of every block.attn) and mlp_params (the parameters of every block.mlp), keep matrix_params as their union so the parameter-count assertion stays true, and build the Muon groups so that attention groups keep lr=matrix_lr while MLP groups use lr=matrix_lr * 1.5. The AdamW groups and everything outside setup_optimizer stay as they are.
coder.title: Larger Muon lr for the MLP matrices

coder.spec: Train the value-embedding gates with AdamW instead of Muon. Each block that has a value embedding owns a tiny ve_gate Linear (n_kv_head x 32 weight) that setup_optimizer currently hands to the Muon groups together with the big block matrices. In GPT.setup_optimizer collect those weights in a list named ve_gate_params, exclude exactly those tensors from matrix_params, add the list to the parameter-count assertion, and give it an AdamW group (lr=scalar_lr, betas=adam_betas, eps=1e-10, weight_decay=0.0). Nothing outside setup_optimizer changes.
coder.title: Value-embedding gates on AdamW

coder.spec: Add an input-dependent output gate per attention head (gated attention). In CausalSelfAttention.__init__ add self.attn_gate = nn.Linear(self.ve_gate_channels, self.n_head, bias=False). In forward, after the flash attention call and before y is flattened, multiply y (shape B, T, n_head, head_dim) by 2 * torch.sigmoid(self.attn_gate(x[..., :self.ve_gate_channels])).unsqueeze(-1). Zero-initialise attn_gate.weight in GPT.init_weights so every gate starts at exactly 1.0 (the model is built on the meta device). attn_gate is an ordinary 2-D matrix inside transformer.h, so setup_optimizer needs no change.
coder.title: Gated attention per head

coder.spec: Add U-Net style skip connections with learned weights. In GPT.__init__ add self.skip_weights = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(config.n_layer // 2)). In GPT.forward let n_skip = n_layer // 2: the outputs of the first n_skip blocks are appended to a list named skips; each of the last n_skip blocks first adds the most recent unused entry, x = x + self.skip_weights[j] * skips.pop(), where j = i - (n_layer - n_skip) is the block's position within the last n_skip blocks, before running the block. Fill skip_weights with 0.0 in GPT.init_weights (meta device). skip_weights lives outside transformer.h, so setup_optimizer's parameter-count assertion fails until you collect it in a list named skip_params, add that list to the assertion, and give it an AdamW group (lr=scalar_lr, betas=adam_betas, eps=1e-10, weight_decay=0.0).
coder.title: U-Net skip connections

coder.spec: Share one value-embedding table across all layers instead of giving every value-embedding layer its own. In GPT.__init__ replace the ModuleDict self.value_embeds with a single table self.value_embed = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, kv_dim). In GPT.forward look it up once before the block loop, ve_all = self.value_embed(idx), and give block i ve = ve_all if has_ve(i, self.config.n_layer) else None. Every other use of self.value_embeds must switch to the single table: the uniform init and the bfloat16 cast in GPT.init_weights, estimate_flops, num_scaling_params and setup_optimizer (value_embeds_params = list(self.value_embed.parameters())). No reference to self.value_embeds may remain. has_ve and the ve_gate layers stay as they are.
coder.title: One shared value-embedding table

coder.spec: Add a zero-initialised residual linear layer just before the output head. In GPT.__init__ add self.pre_head = nn.Linear(config.n_embd, config.n_embd, bias=False). In GPT.forward, right after the final x = norm(x) and before softcap = 15, add x = x + self.pre_head(x). Zero its weight in GPT.init_weights (meta device). pre_head is a plain 2-D matrix outside transformer.h, so make setup_optimizer treat it as a Muon matrix: extend matrix_params with list(self.pre_head.parameters()) so that the parameter-count assertion holds without further change.
coder.title: Zero-initialised linear before the head

coder.spec: Add a multi-token-prediction auxiliary loss. In GPT.__init__ add self.mtp_head = nn.Linear(config.n_embd, config.vocab_size, bias=False) and initialise its weight in GPT.init_weights exactly like lm_head (normal, mean 0.0, std 0.001). In GPT.forward, when targets is not None and reduction == 'mean', compute aux logits from the final hidden state x with the same softcap as the main logits (aux = softcap * torch.tanh(self.mtp_head(x).float() / softcap)) and add 0.3 * F.cross_entropy(aux[:, :-1].reshape(-1, aux.size(-1)), targets[:, 1:].reshape(-1), ignore_index=-1) to the loss: position t then predicts token t+2. The 'none' reduction used for evaluation and the targets=None path must stay exactly as they are. mtp_head lives outside transformer.h, so extend lm_head_params in setup_optimizer with list(self.mtp_head.parameters()) so the parameter-count assertion holds and it trains in the lm_head AdamW group.
coder.title: Multi-token prediction head

coder.spec: Make the rotary base a configurable hyperparameter and raise it to 50000. Add the field rope_base: int = 10000 to GPTConfig, add a module-level hyperparameter ROPE_BASE = 50000 right after WINDOW_PATTERN, pass rope_base=ROPE_BASE in build_model_config, and make the rotary tables use base=config.rope_base. The tables are computed in two places (GPT.__init__ and again in GPT.init_weights), and both must use it.
coder.title: Rotary base as a config field

coder.spec: Expose the second-moment decay of NorMuon (beta2 in the Muon parameter groups, now hard-coded to 0.95) as a hyperparameter and lower it to 0.9. Add MUON_BETA2 = 0.9 to the hyperparameter block right after WEIGHT_DECAY. Give GPT.setup_optimizer a new keyword argument muon_beta2=0.95 at the end of its signature and use it as beta2 in the Muon groups. In the setup_optimizer call in the setup section pass muon_beta2=MUON_BETA2. The Muon momentum, MuonAdamW and everything else stay as they are.
coder.title: Muon beta2 as a hyperparameter

coder.spec: Add a short causal depthwise convolution on the value path. In CausalSelfAttention.__init__ add self.v_conv = nn.Conv1d(kv, kv, kernel_size=3, groups=kv, bias=False) with kv = self.n_kv_head * self.head_dim. In forward, right after v is computed and before the value-embedding mix, replace v by self.v_conv(F.pad(v.view(B, T, -1).transpose(1, 2), (2, 0))).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, T, self.n_kv_head, self.head_dim). The model is built on the meta device, so in GPT.init_weights set every v_conv.weight to the identity filter (all zeros except a 1.0 on the last tap, weight[:, :, -1]). The conv weights are 3-D tensors inside transformer.h, which setup_optimizer currently hands to Muon: collect them in a list named conv_params, exclude them from matrix_params, add the list to the parameter-count assertion, and give it an AdamW group (lr=scalar_lr, betas=adam_betas, eps=1e-10, weight_decay=0.0).
coder.title: Causal depthwise conv on the values

coder.spec: Give the MLP input projection a bias. In MLP.__init__ build c_fc with bias=True (c_proj stays bias-free). nn.Linear leaves its bias uninitialised on the meta device, so zero every block.mlp.c_fc.bias in GPT.init_weights. The biases are 1-D tensors inside transformer.h, which setup_optimizer currently hands to Muon (Muon needs 2-D matrices): collect them in a list named fc_bias_params, exclude them from matrix_params, add the list to the parameter-count assertion, and give it an AdamW group (lr=scalar_lr, betas=adam_betas, eps=1e-10, weight_decay=0.0).
coder.title: Bias on the MLP input projection

coder.spec: Drop the MLP from the last transformer block, so the final layer is attention only. In Block.__init__ create the MLP only when layer_idx < config.n_layer - 1 and set self.mlp = None otherwise. In Block.forward skip the MLP residual update when self.mlp is None. In GPT.init_weights skip the MLP initialisation for a block whose mlp is None. setup_optimizer needs no change, because the remaining MLP parameters still live in transformer.h.
expect: self\.mlp is not None|self\.mlp is None|if self\.mlp:
block\.mlp is not None|block\.mlp is None|block\.mlp\s*:
coder.title: No MLP in the last block

coder.spec: Add a learnable per-channel gain after the final RMS norm. In GPT.__init__ add self.final_gain = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(config.n_embd)). In GPT.forward multiply the output of the final norm (the x = norm(x) that follows the block loop, just before softcap = 15) by it: x = norm(x) * self.final_gain. Fill final_gain with 1.0 in GPT.init_weights (meta device). Train it in the lm_head AdamW group by extending lm_head_params in setup_optimizer with [self.final_gain], so the parameter-count assertion holds without further change.
expect: x = norm\(x\) \* self\.final_gain|x = self\.final_gain \* norm\(x\)|x = norm\(x\)\n\s*(x = x \* self\.final_gain|x = self\.final_gain \* x|x \*= self\.final_gain)\b
coder.title: Learnable gain after the final norm
